o.norm: 64 values Enum (to test whether no int<->long jdk conversion issue exists)

i.norm:
Tests {@link EnumUtils#processBitVector(Class, long)}, which decodes a {@code long} bit vector back into the {@link EnumSet} of enum constants it represents.

Each enum constant maps to the bit at its ordinal position: ordinal 0 -> bit 0 (value 1), ordinal 1 -> bit 1 (value 2), and so on.
Traffic has three constants: RED (ordinal 0, bit 1), AMBER (ordinal 1, bit 2), GREEN (ordinal 2, bit 4). Exercise every combination from the bit vector 0..7.
Enum64 has 64 constants, so the highest bits use the full width of a long. This guards against any int<->long conversion issue when shifting near bit 63.
Long.MIN_VALUE has only the sign bit (bit 63) set, so it equals 1L << 63.
